name: Polymarket
positioning: Self-titled "The World's Largest Prediction Market" (page title tag, observed 2026-07-12). Positions as a news/information product rather than a trading terminal — "forecasting the news": homepage reads like a live news feed of probabilities (topical chips like Trump, Iran, Wimbledon, Fed; a "Breaking" section and dedicated event hubs like /iran). Crypto-native rails (USDC on Polygon, auto-converted to its pUSD stable unit per 2026 guides) but chain is deliberately invisible in the UI. 2025-26 strategic arc: acquired CFTC-licensed QCEX for $112M (Jul 2025) to create QCX LLC / "Polymarket US" DCM; filed Apr 28, 2026 to let US users onto the main exchange; new CFTC probe reported Jun 2026. Monetization shifted in 2026 from ~zero fees to category-based taker fees (geopolitics still free) plus new products observed on the homepage: "Perps are here... leverage up to 20x" and "Build a combo" (parlays). Scale signals are pushed everywhere: "$4,179,028,055 Vol." on the World Cup Winner event alone, "Hot topics" ranked by "$85M today".
visualLanguage: Observed (dark context): near-black charcoal canvas, white primary text, muted gray metadata, one saturated blue accent for all primary actions (Sign Up, Trade, links, chart lines) — a restrained 4-color system where green=Yes/long and red=No/short do the semantic work. Filled green "Buy Yes 38.5¢" vs red "Buy No 61.6¢" pill-ish rectangles on outcome rows. Market imagery everywhere: per-market thumbnails (satellite photo for Strait of Hormuz, team flags, headshots), category icons with their own accents (gold World Cup ball, purple Combos). Charts are thin-line with dotted horizontal gridlines, %-scale, month ticks, a subtle Polymarket watermark, and colored legend dots per outcome (France blue, Argentina yellow...). Big animated odometer-style "8% chance" numeral with red/green delta chips (▼45%). Status ornaments: LIVE badges, live scores inline (Norway 1-1 England, "HT"), flame icons on hot topics, gift icons marking reward-eligible markets, trophy icon beside volume. Density is high — homepage mixes a hero live-sports module, promo tiles, hot-topic list, chip rows, and an "All markets" grid.
typographyBrand: Logotype is a custom geometric sans with subtly rounded corners plus an abstract polygonal mark (nod to Polygon chain); Brandfetch lists Inter as the primary product typeface (secondary source — not verified via computed styles). Hierarchy is weight- and size-driven on one family: bold white market questions (~24-32px), the probability as the largest element on the page ("8% chance", row-level "38%"), small gray caps-ish labels for metadata (PRICE / SHARES / TOTAL in the order book). Numerals do the branding: tabular, abbreviated volume ("$4B Vol.", "$15,070,891 Vol."), dual price encoding — percent for reading probability, cents (38.5¢) for trading — used consistently from card to ticket. Trademark ™ in the title, but the visual tone is sober fintech, not gambling neon.
navigationDiscovery: Desktop top bar: logo, oversized global search ("Search polymarkets..." with "/" keyboard hint), "How it works" (ⓘ), Log In, blue Sign Up, hamburger. Second row splits featured destinations (Trending, World Cup with gold icon, Combos, Breaking) from a scrollable category rail (Politics, Sports/live, Crypto, Esports, Iran, Finance, Geopolitics, Tech, Culture, Economy, Weather, Mentions) with a chevron scroller — note event-specific tabs ("Iran") sit beside evergreen categories. Homepage discovery stack: hero carousel of a featured live event with inline spread/total sub-markets; right rail with product promos (Perps, Combos) and "Hot topics" ranked by today's volume; a row of ~27 topical chips (All, Trump, UFC 329, GTA VI, Tweet Markets...); then the "All markets" infinite grid with search/filter/bookmark icons and "Show more markets". Event pages add: breadcrumb (Economy · Strait Of Hormuz → topic hub /predictions/strait-of-hormuz), date-laddered sibling chips ("Past ▾ | Jul 7 | Jul 15 | Jul 31 | Aug 31 | More ▾"), a related-markets rail filtered by chips (All | Iran | Geopolitics | Politics | Oil), and an SEO FAQ block auto-written per market. Mobile web: bottom tab bar Home / Search / Breaking / More.
marketCardAnatomy: Three observed card species. (1) Multi-outcome card: question title, top 2 outcomes each as a row [name, %, mini Yes/No buttons showing both sides' implied %], aggregate volume ("$4B Vol."), thumbnail. (2) Sports match card: two teams with win % and logos, tri-button Norway/DRAW/England, live score + period ("1 – 1", "HT") or start time, league tag, volume; hero version adds Spread (ENG -1.5 / NOR +1.5) and Total (O 3.5 / U 3.5) selectors with stepper arrows. (3) Binary card: question, large "47% chance", Yes/No buttons, volume. Featured homepage cards can embed recent user comments (social proof). Event-page anatomy in order: breadcrumb + title + utility icons (embed </>, copy-link, bookmark); date-variant chips; big % + delta; multi-line chart with legend, time tabs (1H/6H/1D/1W/1M/ALL); "$… Vol." + close date; outcome table rows [flag/photo, name, per-outcome volume, gift (rewards) icon, big %, green ▲/red ▼ delta, Buy Yes xx.x¢ / Buy No xx.x¢]; collapsed "Order Book" accordion (tabs Trade Yes / Trade No / Rewards; columns PRICE/SHARES/TOTAL; asks stacked above a "Last: 8¢ / Spread: 1¢" divider, bids below); "Rules"; "Market Context" (editorial/AI-flavored situation summary + "Updated Jun 1 — This market's language has been updated for clarity"); Resolver (0x-address) + "Propose resolution"; then community tabs.
tradeTicketClarity: Sticky right-rail card, persistent while scrolling. Header: market thumbnail + truncated title + selected outcome in color ("France · Yes" in green). Buy/Sell as underlined tabs; order-type dropdown top-right (Market ▾ / Limit ▾ — selection persisted across page navigation when observed). Market mode: two large price buttons "Yes 8¢" (green fill when active) / "No 93¢"; "Amount" with a giant $0 placeholder; quick-add chips +$1 +$5 +$10 +$100; full-width blue "Trade"; legal microcopy "By trading, you agree to the Terms of Use." Limit mode swaps to: "Limit price" −/+ cent stepper, "Shares" input with −100/−10/+10/+100/+200 chips, "Expires: Never ▾", then a summary block "Total $0.00" and "To win ⓘ 💵 $0.00" in green. Strengths: one-field market orders, $1-per-winning-share model reinforced by "To win", prices in cents matching the order book. Gaps: no fee line was visible on the observed ticket (that market is in the fee-free geopolitics category; fee-charging categories per docs compute fees at match time — I could not confirm a fee row is shown pre-trade), and no spread/slippage indicator in Market mode even though Yes+No summed to 101¢ on the observed market.
trustRiskSafety: Resolution transparency is the flagship trust surface: every market carries verbatim Rules naming a primary source with URL (IMF Portwatch), thresholds, revision/edge-case handling, fallback timing, plus "Market Opened" timestamp, a Resolver contract address, and a live "Propose resolution" button — the UMA optimistic-oracle process surfaced in-product (help docs: anyone proposes with a USDC.e bond, ~2h unchallenged resolution; disputes → new round → UMA DVM token vote, 4-6 days). Fees: taker-only, maker-free, category-based (docs: fee = shares × rate × p × (1−p); crypto 0.07 rate down to geopolitics 0.00; ~$0.75-$1.80 per 100 shares at 50/50 per third-party tables; deposits/withdrawals free; maker/taker rebate programs) — but the fee matrix lives in docs, not obviously in the trade flow. Risk disclosure is thin: just "By trading, you agree to the Terms of Use" under the ticket and footer notes that "Polymarket operates globally through separate legal entities" with CFTC-regulated US operations; a "Market Integrity" footer link; anti-manipulation/insider rules extended across platforms Mar 2026 (press). No deposit limits, loss limits, cool-offs, or self-exclusion found anywhere on the global product (also absent from help-center search results). Access control is IP geoblocking (~33 countries blocked; orders rejected server-side), with KYC expanding under sanctions/regulatory pressure (Jun 2026 CFTC probe). Comment area shows a "Beware of external links." banner but moderation is evidently light.
socialCommunity: Deep and load-bearing. Community block on every market: Comments (3,721 on the observed market) with the killer detail of position badges on commenters ("Bertapotamous — 233.9K No", "Shiny-Mark — 58.3K Yes") so talk is weighted by skin in the game; "Holders" filter to hide non-position chatter; sort (Newest), replies, likes; observed content ranged from sourced geopolitical updates to an unmoderated threat ("finna snap your fat little neck") left standing with a like. Adjacent tabs: Top Holders (largest Yes/No holders), Positions, Activity (live trade tape). Public trader profiles with P&L feed a Leaderboard page (Monthly / All Categories / Profit/Loss filters, top-20 pagination, "Biggest wins" section; top monthly P&L +$2.89M) — but unclaimed accounts appear as raw wallet strings ("0x2c33...-1759935795465"). Distribution/social-proof mechanics: comments embedded on homepage feature cards, hot-topics ranked by daily volume with flame icons, bookmark/watchlist, copy-link and </> embed widget per market, "Mentions"/Tweet-markets category tying markets to X discourse, news-source attributions (Reuters, AP, BBC) on featured markets.
mobileUsability: Mobile web (observed at 375×812): bottom tab bar Home / Search / Breaking / More; sticky top bar reduced to logo + Sign Up; category chips scroll horizontally; event page stacks legend → chart (time tabs compressed to 1H 1D 1W 1M MAX) → outcome rows with large full-width paired Buy Yes / Buy No buttons (comfortable thumb targets); the desktop side ticket disappears — tapping a buy button presumably opens a sheet (not verified logged-out). Native apps (secondary sources, 2026): iOS 4.7★ (~31K ratings) vs Android 3.8★ (~7K) — a notable platform quality gap; push notifications for price alerts, new markets, and resolution updates; biometric login; trade in "a handful of taps"; US iOS waitlist dropped May 12, 2026 while Android remained waitlist-gated; recurring complaints are withdrawal speed and support responsiveness, not trading UX.
learnFrom: Probability-first card grammar: the % is the hero number everywhere, with dual encoding — % to read, ¢ to trade — kept perfectly consistent from card to order book to ticket

Rules live on the market page itself: named primary source with URL, thresholds, edge cases, fallback timing, market-open timestamp, and a visible resolution/dispute affordance — plus a changelog note ('Updated Jun 1 ... updated for clarity') when wording changes
Position badges on comments ('233.9K No') + a Holders-only filter — cheap, powerful credibility weighting for community discussion
Progressive disclosure of trading complexity: Market order = one amount field + Trade; order book and Limit mode (price stepper, shares, expiry) are collapsed/opt-in
'To win $X' payout preview and the $1-redemption mental model repeated in ticket, FAQ, and docs — teaches the instrument without a tutorial
Date-laddered sibling markets as chips (Jul 7 / Jul 15 / Jul 31 / Aug 31 / Past ▾) — one canvas for deadline-series questions instead of N orphan pages
Volume + close date as the two universal trust numbers on every surface, aggressively abbreviated ($4B Vol.)
Live sports cards with inline score/period and tri-outcome buttons; LIVE badges and 'Hot topics' ranked by today's dollar volume as social proof
Taker-only, maker-free fees with a fee-free civic category — preserves a 'free' headline while monetizing flow; rebates recycle fees to liquidity
Auto-generated per-market FAQ/SEO blocks and an embeddable market widget (</> icon) — every market is a distribution asset
Sticky, context-aware ticket that carries the selected outcome (name + side, color-coded) so the user always knows what they're about to buy
Mobile bottom-tab with a dedicated Breaking tab — commits to the news-first framing on the smallest screen
avoid: No spread/slippage surfacing in the default Market ticket even when Yes+No sums past 100¢ (observed 8¢ + 93¢) — newcomers can't see the cost of crossing the spread
Fee opacity: category-based fees exist in docs but no fee line was visible in the observed pre-trade ticket; a fee matrix that lives only in developer docs erodes trust
Zero responsible-use tooling (no deposit/loss limits, cool-offs, self-exclusion) on a product with gambling-adjacent mechanics — both a trust gap and a regulatory exposure
Light-touch comment moderation: threats and troll replies left standing with likes; a 'Beware of external links.' banner is not a safety system
Raw crypto plumbing leaking into consumer surfaces: resolver shown as a bare 0x address, wallet-string usernames on the public leaderboard, 'Propose resolution' with no explanation layer
Upselling 20x leveraged perps in the same rail as prediction markets — blurs very different risk tiers at the moment of onboarding
Nav taxonomy sprawl: ephemeral event tabs (Iran, UFC 329, Graham Platner) mixed with evergreen categories goes stale and pushes cognitive load onto the chip row
Homepage overload: hero carousel + promos + hot topics + 27 chips + card grid all compete; at least three different card grammars on one screen
Heavy SPA fragility: blank first paints, scroll jank/timeouts in automation, and event pages that break plain HTTP fetches (header overflow) — bad for SEO, embeds, and low-end devices
Platform quality gap (iOS 4.7★ vs Android 3.8★) and waitlist asymmetry — parity matters if community is the moat
Prices that sum to >100% across sibling date-ladder markets with no arbitrage/consistency explanation for casual users
evidenceNotes: DIRECT EVIDENCE (live site in browser pane, 2026-07-12, logged out, desktop 1280×720 + mobile 375×812): homepage nav/hero/promos/hot-topics/card grid and card contents; binary event page (Strait of Hormuz Jul 31) including full Rules text, Market Context block, Resolver address + 'Propose resolution', order book contents (PRICE/SHARES/TOTAL, Last 8¢, Spread 1¢), Market vs Limit ticket fields and chips, comments with position badges and counts, FAQ block, related-market chips; multi-outcome event page (World Cup Winner) outcome rows, deltas, per-outcome volume, $4.18B volume figure; leaderboard page filters and entries; mobile bottom tab bar and stacked layout. WebFetch worked on the homepage and docs.polymarket.com but consistently failed on polymarket.com event subpages ('Parse Error: Header overflow') — the browser pane was used instead, so on-site claims are observed, not fabricated. CAVEATS ON DIRECT OBSERVATION: pages rendered in dark theme — I did not verify whether light theme is the logged-out default (assumption: theme followed the headless browser's color scheme); chart canvases sometimes captured blank and scrolling occasionally hung, so some layout details came from DOM text extraction rather than pixels; logged-in surfaces (portfolio, deposit flow, actual order placement) were NOT tested. INFERENCE: fee display absence in the ticket generalizes from one fee-free geopolitics market — fee-charging categories may show a fee row I didn't see; 'tapping Buy on mobile opens a bottom sheet' is inferred, not observed; Inter as UI typeface comes from Brandfetch, not computed styles. SECONDARY SOURCES (not independently verified): fee rates/formula and rebates (official docs — high confidence), UMA dispute timelines (help center + explainers), QCEX/$112M/CFTC filing dates and Jun-2026 probe (press), App Store ratings and waitlist dates (review sites/App Store), pUSD auto-conversion and MoonPay/Apple Pay deposit details (2026 affiliate guides — moderate confidence, often stale). Volume figures are as-displayed on site and not audited.
